newsitem.title: USA: Actor Brian Keith shoots himself in Malibu.
newsitem.headline: Actor Brian Keith shoots himself in Malibu.

text.p: Actor Brian Keith, who co-starred in the 1961 Disney movie "The Parent Trap" and was well-known for the TV sit-com "Family Affair", shot and killed himself on Tuesday, a sheriff's spokesman said.
Sgt. Noel Lanier said Keith, 75, was found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound in his home in the movie star colony of Malibu, overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
The officer said homicide detectives who went to the house had classified the death as a suicide.
There was no immediate comment from Keith's publicist, Bob Schiller, at Guild Management, but local KCAL television cited a source as saying the actor had been suffering from cancer and emphysema.
In recent years, Keith had been doing "voice-over" work on TV commercials. Paul Doherty, who worked with Keith at a talent agency specialising in this work, said the actor had been not well recently.
"But he wasn't too upfront with us about what was wrong. He kept telling us he didn't feel well," said Doherty.
The sheriff's department said Keith's body was found by family members but he had no further details on the weapon or the fatal wound.
Keith was born in Bayonne, New Jersey, on Nov. 14, 1921 to actor parents, Robert Keith and Helena Shipman, who were members of a touring company.
After serving in the U.S. Marines in the Second World War, he went into stock theatre and radio and also appeared on Broadway in "Mr. Roberts" and "Darkness at Noon".
On film, the burly actor appeared with Hayley Mills, Maureen O'Hara and Leo Carroll in "The Parent Trap" in which Mills played twins who get their divorced parents to remarry.

Keith appeared in more than 80 films, including "Arrowhead", with Charlton Heston, "The Russians are Coming, The Russians are Coming!", Reflections in a Golden Eye", "Nevada Smith" and "The Wind and the Lion" in which he played President Theodore Roosevelt.
In his career he played opposite some of Hollywood's greatest leading ladies -- Barbara Stanwyck, Ginger Rogers, Bette Davis, Kim Novak, O'Hara and Elizabeth Taylor.

He also starred in a number of short-lived TV series, including "The Westerner" (1960), "Archer" (1975), "Hardcastle & McCormick" (1983-1986), "Pursuit of Happiness (1987-1988) and "Heartland" (1989).
But he was best known to TV viewers for "Family Affair", which ran from 1966-71. He played Bill Davis, a swinging Manhattan bachelor with an English butler, Mr. French, played by Sebastian Cabot.
His life was turned upside down when his brother on the show died and he was called on to raise the three orphaned children -- twins Buffy and Jody, and 15-year-old Cissy.
The actress who played Buffy on the programme, Anissa Jones, later died of a drug overdose.

Keith also brought his trademark low-key humour and easygoing style to his role as pediatrician Dr. Sean Jamison on the series "The Brian Keith Show." The show, titled "The Little People" during its first season, ran on NBC from the fall of 1972 through August of 1974.
